about: Every unitary perfect number is even. The route: write σ*(n) for the sum of all unitary divisors of n, n itself included. A unitary perfect n has σ*(n) = 2n. σ* is multiplicative, and σ*(p^k) = 1 + p^k. If n were odd, split off one prime power, n = p^k·m: then 2n = (1 + p^k)·σ*(m). Both factors are even when m > 1, so 4 divides 2n and n is even after all; when m = 1, 1 + p^k = 2p^k forces p^k = 1. Either way a contradiction.
checked: With the five steps taken as given, Lean accepts this proof of the target (shared-run/steps/1052.even_of_isUnitaryPerfect.lean).

steps.plain: A unitary perfect number's unitary divisors, n itself included, add up to 2n.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnitaryPerfect n) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (n / d)), d = 2 * n

steps.plain: The sum of unitary divisors is multiplicative: for coprime a and b, σ*(ab) = σ*(a)·σ*(b). The hardest step.
steps.statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) : ∑ d ∈ (a * b).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a * b / d)), d = (∑ d ∈ a.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a / d)), d) * (∑ d ∈ b.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (b / d)), d)

steps.plain: A prime power p^k (k ≥ 1) has exactly two unitary divisors, 1 and p^k.
steps.statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) : ∑ d ∈ (p ^ k).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (p ^ k / d)), d = 1 + p ^ k

steps.plain: Any n > 1 splits off one prime power: n = p^k·m with k ≥ 1 and p^k coprime to m.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ∃ p k m : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 0 < k ∧ (p ^ k).Coprime m ∧ n = p ^ k * m

steps.plain: An odd number above 1 has an even sum of unitary divisors.
steps.statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : Odd m) (h1 : 1 < m) : Even (∑ d ∈ m.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (m / d)), d)
